chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) sacrificed for the Mothers of the Believers, one cow at a time, and he himself slaughtered sixty-six camels, and Ali (peace be upon him) slaughtered thirty-four camels. He did not give the butchers any of its hides, nor its necklaces, nor its skins, but rather he gave it in charity.

key_terms.بَدَنَةً: Camel (specifically a mature female camel used for sacrifice)

ai.seo_question: How many animals did the Prophet and Imam Ali sacrifice for the Mothers of the Believers, and what happened to their hides?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the specific sacrificial rituals of the Prophet Muhammad and Imam Ali for the 'Mothers of the Believers,' emphasizing the distinct numbers of camels and cows involved. It highlights a key juristic principle regarding *udhiyah*: the carcasses were given entirely in charity rather than used to pay the butchers, illustrating the distinction between ritual sacrifice and commercial transaction in Shia fiqh.
